welcome.autosave:
Your desktop stories are saved in Documents/Twine Studio/Stories by default. Use Show Library to find them. Keep exported backups of important work.

To bring in an existing story, use Import From File in the library. Studio does not automatically migrate your original Twine library.
welcome.browserStorage:
That means you don't need to create an account to use Twine 2, and everything you create isn't stored on a server somewhere else—it stays right in your browser.

Two very important things to remember, though. Since your work is saved only in your browser, if you clear its saved data, then you'll lose your work! Not good. Remember to use that Archive button often. You can also publish individual stories to files using the menu on each story in the story list. Both archive and story files can always be re-imported into Twine.

Secondly, anyone who can use this browser can see and make changes to your work. So if you've got a nosy kid brother, look into setting up a separate profile for yourself.
welcome.browserStorageTitle: Your work is only saved in your browser
welcome.done: Thanks for reading, and have fun with Twine.
welcome.greeting:
Welcome to Twine Studio, an independent fork of Twine. Write a passage, add choices, and play your story.

You can start writing immediately. AI is not required. This fork is not endorsed by the Twine project.
welcome.help: If you've never used Twine before, then welcome! The Twine Cookbook is a great resource for learning how to use it. If you haven't used Twine before, it's a great place to start.

storage.savingHelp: Your changes are protected while the browser finishes saving.
storage.ambiguousDraftHelp: Studio kept every version and did not choose one for you. Export recovery data before continuing this story.
storage.discardDraftWarning: This may be the only copy of this writing. Export recovery data or copy the text before discarding it.
storage.draftRemoved: Draft removed. Reload after saving or exporting any other unsaved writing to refresh recovery status.
storage.draftNotRemoved: This draft changed or browser storage could not remove it. Review the current text before trying again.
storage.conflictHelp: This tab stopped saving to protect the newer saved version. Your work here is still open. Export a story backup, then reload to see the other tab's changes. Re-import your backup if you want to recover this tab's draft.
storage.draftConflictTitle: Recovered writing differs from the saved story
storage.draftConflictHelp: Your writing from before reload is open here, but the saved passage also changed. Export a story backup before choosing to discard this recovered draft and open the saved version.
storage.discardRecoveredDraft: Discard recovered draft and open saved version
storage.orphanDraftTitle: Recovered writing has no saved passage
storage.orphanDraftHelp: A passage or story was removed while this tab had unsaved writing. Export recovery data before discarding that draft; the story backup may not contain it.
storage.unreadableStoryTitle: Some saved writing could not be opened
storage.unreadableStoryHelp: Studio stopped saving stories because a listed story or passage is missing or unreadable. Keep this tab open and export recovery data before repairing storage. A story backup includes only the writing that could be opened; export one before reloading if you made more edits.
storage.keepOpen: Your latest changes are still in this window. Keep it open, export a backup, then free browser storage and retry. Reloading may lose unsaved changes.
storage.recovered: Recovered changes are loaded from a saved journal. Retry saving to finish recovery, or export a backup first.
storage.loadFailed: Your saved work could not be opened
storage.preserve: Keep your saved data. Export recovery data before clearing storage or reinstalling.

fact.help: Append a fact, numeric change or conditional choice to this passage. These actions run every time the reader visits, in source order.
fact.name: Fact name
fact.conditionHelp: Remember this fact's starting value in the first passage before using it in a condition. Use the same name and value type throughout. A new destination will be created if needed.
fact.dialogueHelp: Set this fact before checking it. This inserts one short plain-text line when the condition is true; edit the passage source for longer or formatted dialogue.
fact.changeHelp: Set this fact to a number before changing it, usually in your start passage. Each visit applies the change again. Keep its name and number type consistent.
fact.nameHelp: Use a short name such as clue or trust: start with a letter, then use letters, numbers or underscores (up to 40 characters). Numbers may range from -1 billion to 1 billion.
fact.invalid: Check the fact name, value and any choice fields. Choice text and destination must use plain text.

choice.help: Add one or more choices at the end of this passage. Your reader will see the choice text.
choice.label: Choice text
choice.existing: This choice will lead to the existing passage.
choice.new: A new passage will be created for you.
choice.plainText: Use plain words, numbers, spaces, and punctuation. Use the source editor for special syntax.
choice.unsupported: The choice helper supports Harlowe 3 and SugarCube 2. You can still write links directly in the source for this format.
